paras.text: Topic: 地點、方位 places and directions
• Say where a person or a place is, and whether it is near or far.
• Name what is around a place: in front, behind, inside, outside, next to, nearby.
• Give a short comment on what a place looks like.
Practice dialogue written for this site with the vocabulary of Dialogue I. The book’s own Dialogue I is on book p. 104 (PDF p. 131); its recording is track 06-01.

lines.zh: 聽說你朋友現在在花蓮。
lines.py: Tīngshuō nǐ péngyǒu xiànzài zài Huālián.

lines.zh: 是啊，她家在花蓮的山上。
lines.py: Shì a, tā jiā zài Huālián de shānshàng.

lines.zh: 山上？遠不遠？
lines.py: Shānshàng? Yuǎn bù yuǎn?

lines.zh: 有一點遠，可是那裡的風景真的很美，附近也有海。
lines.py: Yǒu yìdiǎn yuǎn, kěshì nàlǐ de fēngjǐng zhēnde hěn měi, fùjìn yě yǒu hǎi.

lines.zh: 她的家人也都在那裡嗎？
lines.py: Tā de jiārén yě dōu zài nàlǐ ma?

lines.zh: 對，他們都在那裡。她家前面、後面都是山。
lines.py: Duì, tāmen dōu zài nàlǐ. Tā jiā qiánmiàn, hòumiàn dōu shì shān.

lines.zh: 那是一個很漂亮的地方吧？我很想去看看。
lines.py: Nà shì yí ge hěn piàoliàng de dìfāng ba? Wǒ hěn xiǎng qù kànkàn.

lines.zh: 好啊！這個週末我們一起去。
lines.py: Hǎo a! Zhè ge zhōumò wǒmen yìqǐ qù.

lines.zh: 太好了！你現在要去哪裡？
lines.py: Tài hǎo le! Nǐ xiànzài yào qù nǎlǐ?

lines.zh: 我要去樓下找朋友。你呢？
lines.py: Wǒ yào qù lóuxià zhǎo péngyǒu. Nǐ ne?

lines.zh: 我要去學校上課。
lines.py: Wǒ yào qù xuéxiào shàngkè.

translation.en: I heard your friend is in Hualien now.
Yes, her home is up in the mountains in Hualien.
In the mountains? Is that far?
A little, but the scenery there is truly beautiful, and the sea is close by too.
Is her family there as well?
Yes, they are all there. There are mountains both in front of and behind her house.
It must be a lovely place. I’d really like to go and see it.
Sure! Let’s go together this weekend.
Great! Where are you off to now?
I’m going downstairs to meet a friend. And you?
I’m going to school for class.

items.en: to go and see (someone), to look for
Hualien, a city on Taiwan’s east coast
(I) heard that…, it is said that…

paras.text: Practice dialogue written for this site with the vocabulary of Dialogue II. The book’s own Dialogue II is on book p. 107 (PDF p. 134); its recording is track 06-03.

lines.zh: 這裡是我們學校。
lines.py: Zhèlǐ shì wǒmen xuéxiào.

lines.zh: 你們學校很大！教室在哪裡？
lines.py: Nǐmen xuéxiào hěn dà! Jiàoshì zài nǎlǐ?

lines.zh: 教室在那棟大樓裡面，圖書館在教室旁邊。
lines.py: Jiàoshì zài nà dòng dàlóu lǐmiàn, túshūguǎn zài jiàoshì pángbiān.

lines.zh: 學生宿舍呢？
lines.py: Xuéshēng sùshè ne?

lines.zh: 宿舍在學校後面，很近，很方便。
lines.py: Sùshè zài xuéxiào hòumiàn, hěn jìn, hěn fāngbiàn.

lines.zh: 你們在哪裡吃飯？
lines.py: Nǐmen zài nǎlǐ chīfàn?

lines.zh: 宿舍的一樓有餐廳，學校外面也有很多小吃。
lines.py: Sùshè de yì lóu yǒu cāntīng, xuéxiào wàimiàn yě yǒu hěn duō xiǎochī.

lines.zh: 買東西方便嗎？
lines.py: Mǎi dōngxi fāngbiàn ma?

lines.zh: 很方便。圖書館旁邊有一家商店。
lines.py: Hěn fāngbiàn. Túshūguǎn pángbiān yǒu yì jiā shāngdiàn.

lines.zh: 前面那棟漂亮的大樓呢？
lines.py: Qiánmiàn nà dòng piàoliàng de dàlóu ne?

lines.zh: 那是游泳池。我常在那裡游泳。
lines.py: Nà shì yóuyǒngchí. Wǒ cháng zài nàlǐ yóuyǒng.

translation.en: This is our school.
Your school is big! Where are the classrooms?
The classrooms are in that building, and the library is next to them.
And the student dorms?
The dorms are behind the school — very close and convenient.
Where do you eat?
There’s a restaurant on the first floor of the dorm, and lots of snacks outside the school too.
Is it easy to buy things?
Very. There’s a shop next to the library.
What about that nice building in front?
That’s the swimming pool. I often swim there.

items.en: to have a meal, to eat

blocks.en: I. 在 zài: saying where someone or something is

paras.text: Use: As a verb, 在 zài tells us the location of a person or thing. Pattern: Subject + 在 + place.
The “place” after 在 can be one of three kinds:
A. A word that already names a place: city and country names, or nouns such as 學校, 餐廳, 宿舍, 圖書館.
B. A position word: 上 / 下 / 前 / 後 / 裡 / 外 + 面 or 邊, and also 旁邊 and 附近 (these two take no suffix).
C. Noun + (的) + position word, e.g. 學校（的）後面 “behind the school”.

head: Position word
Meaning
Example
rows: 宿舍前面 in front of the dorm
學校後面 behind the school
教室裡面 in the classroom
圖書館外面 outside the library
商店旁邊 next to the shop
我家附近 near my home

items.en: The teacher is in the classroom now.
The café is next to the library.
The swimming pool is behind the school.

items.py: Wǒ de shū zài sùshè lǐmiàn.
items.en: My books are in the dorm.

items.py: Cāntīng zài bú zài sùshè fùjìn?
items.en: Is the restaurant near the dorm?

paras.text: Usage notes:
1. An ordinary object noun (房子, 書, 手機…) is not a place by itself, so it needs a position word: say 他在房子裡面, not *他在房子.
2. A proper place name (臺灣, 臺北, 花蓮) never takes 裡面: say 他在臺灣, not *他在臺灣裡面. With words like 學校 or 宿舍, adding 裡面 is optional and just stresses “inside”: 他在學校 / 他在學校裡面.
3. The reference point comes first and the position word second: 學校前面 means “in front of the school”, but 前面的學校 means “the school in front” (a description of the school).
4. Short forms are very common: 的 and the suffix 面 are often dropped, e.g. 樓下, 山上, 家裡, 房子裡. These short forms are fixed words, so *樓的下面 is not used for “downstairs”.

blocks.instruction: Answer each question with 在, using the place given in brackets.

items.prompt: 圖書館在哪裡？（教室旁邊）→ ＿＿＿＿＿＿。
你朋友在哪裡？（樓下）→ ＿＿＿＿＿＿。
游泳池在哪裡？（宿舍後面）→ ＿＿＿＿＿＿。
他們學校在哪裡？（花蓮的山上）→ ＿＿＿＿＿＿。
老師在哪裡？（圖書館外面）→ ＿＿＿＿＿＿。

blocks.title: 練習 Exercise
blocks.instruction: Each sentence has one mistake. Rewrite it correctly.

items.prompt: ＊我朋友在臺北裡面。→ ＿＿＿＿＿＿。
＊咖啡店在前面的圖書館。（meaning: The café is in front of the library.）→ ＿＿＿＿＿＿。

blocks.en: II. 有 yǒu: saying what there is in a place

paras.text: Use: 有 can also mean “there is / there are”. The place comes first, then 有, then what is found there. Pattern: Place + 有 + (number + measure word) + noun.
The place part follows the same three types as in Grammar I.

items.zh: 學校附近有一家咖啡店。
items.py: Xuéxiào fùjìn yǒu yì jiā kāfēi diàn.
items.en: There is a café near the school.

items.py: Sùshè lóuxià yǒu hěn duō xuéshēng.
items.en: There are lots of students downstairs in the dorm.

items.py: Wǒ jiā pángbiān yǒu yí dòng dàlóu.
items.en: There is a building next to my home.

items.zh: 圖書館裡面沒有咖啡店。
items.py: Túshūguǎn lǐmiàn méi yǒu kāfēi diàn.
items.en: There is no café in the library.
There is no sea near here.
Are there any students in the classroom?

items.py: Sùshè fùjìn yǒu méi yǒu shāngdiàn?
items.en: Is there a shop near the dorm?

paras.text: Usage notes:

1. A 有 sentence introduces something new or not yet identified (“there is a shop downstairs”). A 在 sentence locates something both speakers already have in mind (“the shop is downstairs”). Compare 樓下有一家商店 with 那家商店在樓下.
2. Two kinds of 有: with a person as subject it means “to have” and takes an object (我有一支手機 “I have a phone”). With a place in front it means “there is” (房子裡面有一支手機 “there is a phone in the house”).

blocks.title: 練習 Exercise
blocks.instruction: Describe each place with 有 (✓) or 沒有 (✗).

items.prompt: 學校附近／咖啡店 ✓ → ＿＿＿＿＿＿。
圖書館旁邊／游泳池 ✗ → ＿＿＿＿＿＿。

blocks.title: 練習 Exercise
blocks.instruction: Put the parts in order to make a sentence.

items.prompt: 附近 ① ／ 有 ② ／ 我家 ③ ／ 一家餐廳 ④ → ＿＿＿＿＿＿。
沒有 ① ／ 山上 ② ／ 商店 ③ → ＿＿＿＿＿＿。
有沒有 ① ／ 宿舍裡面 ② ／ 餐廳 ③ → ＿＿＿＿＿＿？

blocks.en: III. Doubling a verb: V（一）V to soften an action

paras.text: Use: Saying a verb twice makes the action sound light and casual — “just a little”, “have a quick …”. In requests and suggestions it makes you sound more polite and relaxed.
With a one-syllable verb, 一 may be inserted: 看看 or 看一看.

items.en: Let’s go up the mountain and have a look.

items.zh: 你想一想，週末要去哪裡？
items.py: Nǐ xiǎng yì xiǎng, zhōumò yào qù nǎlǐ?
items.en: Have a think — where do you want to go this weekend?

items.zh: 週末我喜歡在家看看書、喝喝茶。
items.py: Zhōumò wǒ xǐhuān zài jiā kànkàn shū, hēhē chá.
items.en: On weekends I like to read a bit and have some tea at home.

items.py: Qǐng nǐ jiāojiāo wǒ, hǎo ma?
items.en: Could you teach me a bit, please?

items.zh: 你要不要去圖書館找找？
items.py: Nǐ yào bú yào qù túshūguǎn zhǎozhǎo?
items.en: Do you want to go and look in the library?

blocks.title: Questions (a tag question, or an A-not-A auxiliary verb)

paras.text: Usage notes:
1. Mostly action verbs can be doubled. From the lessons so far: 看、吃、喝、想、做、打、找、買、教、幫.
2. With a verb + object, only the verb is doubled: 上網 → 上上網, 做飯 → 做做飯, 喝茶 → 喝喝茶.

blocks.title: 練習 Exercise
blocks.instruction: Complete each sentence with a doubled verb.

items.prompt: 那家咖啡店的咖啡很好喝，你可以去＿＿＿＿＿＿。
我不會做甜點，請你＿＿＿＿＿＿我。
我的手機不在這裡，我去樓下＿＿＿＿＿＿。

blocks.en: IV. 不是 búshì: “it isn’t that …”

paras.text: Use: 不是 placed before a statement denies something that was said or assumed: “it’s not the case that…”. It is different from plain 不 and 沒: those negate the action itself, while 不是 rejects an idea. Usually the speaker then gives the correct version.
不是 can come before positive or negative statements.

items.zh: 我們學校不是在臺北，是在花蓮。
items.py: Wǒmen xuéxiào búshì zài Táiběi, shì zài Huālián.
items.en: Our school isn’t in Taipei — it’s in Hualien.

items.zh: 我不是要買咖啡，我要買茶。
items.py: Wǒ búshì yào mǎi kāfēi, wǒ yào mǎi chá.
items.en: It’s not coffee I want to buy; I want tea.

items.zh: 他不是不想去，他今天要上課。
items.py: Tā búshì bù xiǎng qù, tā jīntiān yào shàngkè.
items.en: It’s not that he doesn’t want to go; he has class today.

items.zh: 那家餐廳的菜不是不好吃，是有一點貴。
items.py: Nà jiā cāntīng de cài búshì bù hǎochī, shì yǒu yìdiǎn guì.
items.en: It’s not that the food there isn’t good — it’s just a bit pricey.

paras.text: Compare: 他不去 simply says “he isn’t going”. 他不是要去圖書館，他要去游泳池 corrects a guess: “it’s not the library he’s going to; it’s the pool.”

blocks.title: 練習 Exercise
blocks.instruction: Complete B’s reply with 不是.

items.prompt: A：圖書館在宿舍後面嗎？　B：＿＿＿＿＿＿，在宿舍前面。
A：你不喜歡吃辣的嗎？　B：＿＿＿＿＿＿，我今天不想吃。
A：你要去樓下找朋友嗎？　B：＿＿＿＿＿＿，我要去樓下買東西。
A：那家店的東西很貴嗎？　B：＿＿＿＿＿＿，可是也不便宜。

blocks.en: V. Where an action happens: 在 / 到 + place + action

paras.text: Use: To say where something is done, put 在 (at) or 到 (go to) with the place before the action. Pattern: Subject + 在／到 + place + verb phrase.

items.en: I often read in the library.
He is online in the dorm.

items.zh: 我們到學校附近的餐廳吃飯吧。
items.py: Wǒmen dào xuéxiào fùjìn de cāntīng chīfàn ba.
items.en: Let’s go and eat at a restaurant near the school.

items.py: Tā jīntiān bú zài jiā chīfàn.
items.en: He isn’t eating at home today.

items.zh: 我們不到那家店買東西。
items.py: Wǒmen bú dào nà jiā diàn mǎi dōngxi.
items.en: We don’t go to that shop to buy things.

items.zh: 你要不要到樓下喝咖啡？
items.py: Nǐ yào bú yào dào lóuxià hē kāfēi?
items.en: Do you want to go downstairs for coffee?

paras.text: Usage notes:
1. The place phrase always comes before the verb, as with other prepositional phrases: 他在家學中文, not *他學中文在家.
2. In the negative, 不 normally goes in front of 在／到 rather than the main verb: “He doesn’t go online at home” is 他不在家上網.

items.prompt: 圖書館 ① ／ 他 ② ／ 看書 ③ ／ 在 ④ → ＿＿＿＿＿＿。
到 ① ／ 我們 ② ／ 吃飯 ③ ／ 樓下的餐廳 ④ → ＿＿＿＿＿＿。
不 ① ／ 家 ② ／ 在 ③ ／ 她 ④ ／ 上網 ⑤ → ＿＿＿＿＿＿。
常 ① ／ 你 ② ／ 打籃球 ③ ／ 在哪裡 ④ → ＿＿＿＿＿＿？

paras.text: Goal: Describe where people and places are.

Task: Draw a simple map of your school (or your street) with at least five places on it — e.g. 教室、圖書館、餐廳、商店、宿舍、游泳池. Without showing the map, describe it to a partner using 在 and position words (前面、後面、旁邊、附近…). Your partner draws what you describe. Then compare the two maps.
Goal: Talk about where you live and what is around it.
Task: Ask two classmates the questions below and note their answers. Then tell the class whose neighbourhood sounds most convenient.

paras.text: Goal: Describe a school and its surroundings.
Task: In pairs, find out about each other’s school (in your home country or here). Use the questions below, then report two interesting facts to the class.

items.prompt: 你的學校在哪裡？
你的學校裡面有什麼？
你的學校附近有什麼？風景美不美？
你常在學校附近做什麼？

paras.text: Many people in Taiwan pay attention to how numbers sound. 四 sì “four” sounds close to 死 sǐ “to die”, so it is often avoided: some hospitals and buildings skip the 4th floor, and an address full of 4s can be harder to sell or rent.

Other numbers are welcome for the same reason. 八 bā sounds like 發 fā “to prosper, get rich”, and 六 liù is linked with things going smoothly (as in the saying 六六大順) and with 祿 lù “an official’s salary, good fortune”. Phone numbers, licence plates and prices with 6 and 8 are popular.

Taiwan has one of the lowest birth rates in the world. According to the Ministry of the Interior, about 305,000 babies were born in 2000 but only about 167,000 in 2010; there was a short rise to about 229,000 in 2012 (a Year of the Dragon, considered lucky for births), and the number has kept falling since.
Fewer births mean fewer students a generation later. Many schools and university departments — private ones above all — now struggle to fill places, and some have merged or closed.

blocks.en: Introduction to Chinese Characters — The Six Categories (六書 liùshū)

paras.text: Traditionally, Chinese characters are sorted into six types, called the “six writings”, 六書 liùshū:
1. Pictographs 象形 — simplified drawings of things: 山 mountain, 日 sun, 月 moon, 木 tree.
2. Indicatives 指事 — a sign or mark points to an abstract idea: 上 above, 下 below, 本 “root” (a mark at the bottom of 木 tree).
3. Compound ideographs 會意 — two or more parts combine into a new meaning: 明 bright (日 sun + 月 moon), 休 rest (人 person leaning on 木 a tree), 林 woods (two trees).

4. Phono-semantic compounds 形聲 — one part hints at the meaning, the other at the sound. This is by far the largest group: 媽 mā (女 woman + 馬 mǎ for the sound), 晴 qíng sunny (日 + 青 qīng), 清 qīng clear (水 water + 青).
5. Derivative cognates 轉注 — pairs of related characters that explain each other, such as 考 and 老, both once meaning “old”.
6. Phonetic loans 假借 — a character borrowed for another word that sounded the same. 來, for example, first pictured a kind of wheat and was later borrowed for “to come”.

items: I can say where something is and whether it is near or far.
I can talk about the places around my home, school or workplace.
I can make a simple comment about how a place looks.
